title: H-Index
statement: A researcher has written `citations.length` papers, and `citations[i]` counts how many times paper `i` has been cited. Return the researcher's h-index: the largest integer `h` for which `h` or more of the papers each have a citation count of `h` or higher. When no paper has any citations, the h-index is `0`.
notes:
## Intuition

The answer is at most the number of papers, so a brute force can try every `h` from `n` down and count the papers with at least `h` citations, O(n²) in total. Sorting removes the counting: once the counts are in decreasing order, the first `k` papers are the `k` most cited, and they all have at least `k` citations exactly when the `k`-th one does. So the h-index is the longest prefix where each position's count still covers its 1-based rank.

## Approach

1. Copy `citations` into `sorted`, ordered from most to least cited.
2. Walk the positions `i`; `papers = i + 1` is how many papers the prefix up to `i` holds.
3. If `sorted[i]` is smaller than `papers`, this prefix (and every longer one) fails, so stop.
4. Otherwise `papers` papers all have at least `papers` citations, so set `h = papers`.
5. Return `h`.

## Example 1, step by step

`sorted = [6, 5, 3, 1, 0]`. At `i = 0`, `6 >= 1` so `h = 1`; at `i = 1`, `5 >= 2` so `h = 2`; at `i = 2`, `3 >= 3` so `h = 3`; at `i = 3`, `1 < 4`, so the loop stops and the answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the scan is O(n).
- Space: O(n) for the sorted copy. A counting sort over the counts 0 to n (larger counts all go in bucket n) gives O(n) time.

## Pitfalls

- JavaScript's default `sort` compares numbers as strings (`100` before `9`); always pass a comparator.
- The h-index never exceeds the number of papers, even if every paper is cited 1000 times.
- Compare with the 1-based rank `i + 1`, not `i`, and use `<` for failure: a paper with exactly `h` citations counts.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `sorted` | the citation counts, largest first |
| `i` | position in `sorted` |
| `papers` | how many papers the prefix ending at `i` contains |
| `h` | the largest prefix length confirmed so far |

narration.2: Order the counts from most to least cited so the best papers come first.
narration.3: With no paper checked yet, the h-index is 0.
narration.5: Grow the prefix of top papers one position at a time.
narration.6: The prefix ending here holds i + 1 papers.
narration.7: Does the weakest paper in this prefix have fewer citations than the prefix length?
narration.8: Then no longer prefix can work either, so stop.
narration.10: All papers in the prefix have at least that many citations: it is a valid h.
narration.12: Return the longest prefix that passed.
